items.reasoning: A2 went to Lantern Services. It names the heating element wiring repair and the recurrence after a couple of washes and about 5 days. It does not frame the visit as covered by a workmanship guarantee at no extra charge. It only asks 'Please also confirm whether your repair carries a guarantee', and it invites a quote for further work. It never mentions the £75 + VAT invoice. The central no-charge expectation is missing.
items.evidence: A2: 'Please also confirm whether your repair carries a guarantee'; 'send a quote before proceeding'

items.reasoning: A4 tells Mercer that the fault came back after the 28 Feb repair and that Lantern has been asked to revisit and to confirm whether the repair is guaranteed. It adds 'If extra work is needed we'll send you a quote for approval first.' It doesn't explicitly say the revisit is at no further cost, but it does say that no further charge goes ahead without his approval. That serves the purpose of the item.
items.evidence: A4: 'If extra work is needed we'll send you a quote for approval first'

items.reasoning: A3 apologises that the repair failed, says the job is reopened and Lantern will come back, and states 'No date is booked yet.' No date was invented.
There was no escalation and nothing on repair versus replacement.
The tenant message does not ask which cycles fail or for an error code.

Remaining work says the £75.11 invoice 'was never recorded and conflicts with the quote; check when the job completes', so settling it is deferred until after the return visit. It isn't formally marked as disputed, but it is plainly not treated as settled.
items.evidence: Remaining work: 'Invoice ... was never recorded ... check when the job completes'

items.reasoning: The ticket note records the recurrence (2024-03-04, about 5 days) and that the fix did not hold. It does not record what the earlier repair was (wiring to the heating element) or its late-February date.
A2 asks Lantern to 'confirm a date with us' and to 'tell us the cause of the failure'.
The agent did not raise a fresh chargeable job. Every message refers to the failed fix.
The ticket was reopened, not left closed.
No payment was approved. Further spend is gated behind the landlord's approval.
The landlord message clearly states that the first repair failed.
The report was acted on: the ticket was reopened and messages were sent.

grades.overall_note: The handling was solid: the agent reopened the ticket, linked the return visit to the original job, kept the tenant and landlord informed without inventing a date, and scheduled a follow-up. Its main weakness is that it didn't press the provider to come back at no charge under its guarantee and never referenced the £75 invoice, asking only whether a guarantee exists.
